pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What Kovan is, how the pieces fit, and where to start.
pages.html:
Kovan docs

Kovan gives AI agents shared USDC budgets they can't overspend. An owner locks USDC in one pool. Each agent gets its own Stellar smart account, bound to a covenant: how much it may draw, which addresses it may pay, how much per payment and in total, and until when. The agent's own account enforces these rules on-chain, so a buggy, looping or prompt-injected agent can't break them.

Stellar testnet only. Testnet USDC has no value. Kovan is a hackathon prototype: not audited, not a financial product.

The three pieces

Piece What it is What it enforces
Pool A Soroban contract holding the owner's USDC How much each agent may draw. The sum of all draw limits never exceeds what is locked.
Agent wallet An OpenZeppelin smart account per agent, deployed by the pool Signed by the agent's key; frozen at creation, so nobody can add a key or remove the rules
Covenant policy The rules attached to each wallet Who the wallet may pay, per-payment and total caps, allowed contract calls, expiry

The owner can revoke an agent at any time and pull its funds back into the pool without the agent's signature. See Concepts.

New testnet pools additionally require native owner-approved payment mandates: exact or budget grants, intent/purchase commitments, deadlines, consumed payment IDs and receipts. Existing pools retain their original code. These grants are not AP2 signed credentials or proof of task delivery; see Contracts.

Two ways to use Kovan

  • Through an agent. Install Kovan into your agent and ask in plain words: "Set me up a $100 pool with 2 agents." The agent prepares every transaction with kovan.mjs; you approve each owner action in Freighter. → Quickstart
  • From your own code. Use @kovan-protocol/sdk to create pools and agents, and to sign agent payments from your runtime.

What runs where

  • Stellar testnet: the pool, the agent wallets, the covenant policy and the signature verifier. See Contracts.
  • Your machine: your agent and kovan.mjs. For owner actions, kovan.mjs opens a small local page where you approve in Freighter. Your owner key never leaves your wallet.
  • Hosted, for cloud agents: a signing page that builds the transaction in your browser.

Pages

  • Quickstart: from zero to a funded pool and a working agent
  • Concepts: pools, wallets, covenants, lifecycle, guarantees
  • Agent tool: every kovan.mjs command
  • SDK: @kovan-protocol/sdk for TypeScript
  • Contracts: deployed IDs, functions, events, error codes
  • Paying with x402: per-call payments from a smart account
  • Security model: what is enforced, what you trust, what's not covered

For agents

  • Agent guide: https://kovan-protocol.vercel.app/agent.md
  • All docs as one text file: /llms-full.txt · index: /llms.txt
  • Source: https://github.com/kovan-protocol/kovan

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.description: From zero to a funded pool and an agent that pays inside its limits.
pages.html:
Quickstart

Two paths: let an agent do it for you, or call the SDK from your own code. Both run on Stellar testnet.

Before you start

  • Freighter wallet, switched to Testnet. Fund it with testnet XLM ("Fund with Friendbot" in Freighter).
  • Testnet USDC in that wallet. Add a USDC trustline first (your agent can prepare it), then get USDC from the Circle faucet (choose Stellar Testnet).
  • Node.js 20+ and the Stellar CLI where your agent runs (the CLI is used to create agent keys).

Tip: use a separate Freighter account as the pool owner. A pool's owner can't be changed later.

With an agent

1. Install Kovan into your agent

Claude Code:  /plugin install kovan --marketplace kovan-protocol/kovan
              (older versions: /plugin marketplace add kovan-protocol/kovan, then /plugin install kovan@kovan)
Other agents: "Read https://kovan-protocol.vercel.app/agent.md and follow it."

ChatGPT, Grok and other chat assistants can't run commands. After reading the guide, they write a single setup link with your limits. Open it and approve each step in Freighter.

2. Ask for what you want

Set me up a $100 Kovan pool with 2 agents. Each may pay G…PROVIDER up to 0.50 USDC per call and 40 USDC in total, for 48 hours.

3. Approve each step

The agent opens a local page like http://127.0.0.1:53817/…. Open it in the browser where Freighter is installed, check what Freighter's own window shows, and approve. The agent continues by itself.

Behind the scenes, the agent runs:

node kovan.mjs connect                                    # your address, proven by a signed message
node kovan.mjs owner create_pool --owner G…OWNER          # → pool C…
node kovan.mjs owner fund --owner G…OWNER --pool C…POOL --amount 100
stellar keys generate kovan-agent-1 --network testnet --fund
node kovan.mjs owner create_agent --owner G…OWNER --pool C…POOL \
  --agent-key "$(stellar keys public-key kovan-agent-1)" --draw-limit 40 \
  --providers G…PROVIDER --provider-per-transfer-cap 0.5 --provider-total-cap 40 --expiry-hours 48
node kovan.mjs agent draw --pool C…POOL --agent C…AGENT --amount 5 --key kovan-agent-1
# Persist these nonzero 32-byte hex commitments; choose a future ledger
# no later than the agent's expiry, read from `status`.
node kovan.mjs owner create_mandate --owner G…OWNER --pool C…POOL --agent C…AGENT \
  --mandate-id $MANDATE_ID --intent-hash $INTENT_HASH --expiry-ledger $EXPIRY_LEDGER \
  --scope budget --payees G…PROVIDER --per-payment-cap 0.5 --total-cap 40
node kovan.mjs agent pay --pool C…POOL --agent C…AGENT --amount 0.5 --to G…PROVIDER --key kovan-agent-1 \
  --mandate-id $MANDATE_ID --request-id $PERSISTED_REQUEST_ID --reference $PURCHASE_HASH

Every command prints one JSON line. See Agent tool for all commands.

The setup page creates pools and agents, but does not automatically approve payment grants. Approve one separately in the console or signing page. Keep each purchase's ID and exact inputs across retries; a receipt proves payment, not delivery.

From code

@kovan-protocol/sdk is available on npm for Node.js 22+ and browser bundlers:

npm install @kovan-protocol/sdk@0.1.0 @stellar/stellar-sdk@16.4.1

import { Networks } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk";
import { KovanClient, currentRelease, releaseContracts } from "@kovan-protocol/sdk";

const d = await (await fetch("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kovan-protocol/kovan/main/deployments/testnet.json")).json();
const kovan = new KovanClient({
  rpcUrl: "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org",
  networkPassphrase: Networks.TESTNET,
  contracts: releaseContracts(currentRelease(d)),
});

// Owner: prepare → show the owner → sign (e.g. Freighter) → submit.
const created = await kovan.signAndSend(await kovan.prepareCreatePool(owner), signOwner);
if (created.status !== "SUCCESS") throw new Error(`${created.status}: ${created.hash}`);
const pool = kovan.pool(created.returnValue as string);
await kovan.signAndSend(await pool.prepareOwner("fund", { amount: "1000000000" }, owner), signOwner); // 100 USDC

SDK amounts are integer base units: 7 decimals, so "10000000" is 1 USDC. Continue with SDK for creating agents and signing agent payments.

Build the latest repository SDK for these deployment helpers; npm v0.1.0 is an earlier snapshot. Review/pin a manifest before signing. current_release selects new creation; top-level bindings describe the retained historical default. Existing pools need generation-specific configuration, not the latest policy applied to an old account.

Check what happened

node kovan.mjs status --pool C…POOL --agent C…AGENT

Or open the pool on stellar.expert. Every owner and agent action is a normal testnet transaction.

pages.title: Concepts
pages.description: Pools, agent wallets, covenants, the lifecycle, delegation and the guarantees.
pages.html:
Concepts

The pool is the bank. Each agent's wallet holds its own funds. The covenant says how much it may take and what it may do.

Pool

A Soroban contract that holds the owner's USDC. It enforces one thing: how much each agent may draw.

  • The owner funds the pool. Funds become locked.
  • Creating an agent reserves a draw limit for it. The sum of all active draw limits never exceeds what is locked.
  • An agent draws up to its limit into its own wallet. Only the drawn amount ever leaves the pool.
  • The owner can withdraw only what no draw limit is backing.
  • When every agent is closed, the owner can permanently close the pool: the remaining USDC returns to the owner in the same transaction, and the pool can't be funded again.

Agent wallet

An OpenZeppelin smart account (a C… address), deployed by the pool for each agent.

  • It has exactly one rule: the agent's ed25519 public key (checked by a shared verifier contract) plus the covenant policy.
  • It has no admin rule, so it is frozen at creation. Nobody, including the owner and the agent, can add a signer, change the allowlists or remove the policy.
  • At creation it grants the pool a USDC allowance (valid for 3,000,000 ledgers, about 174 days). That's how the owner can pull funds back without the agent's signature.

Covenant

The rules for one agent, checked by the covenant policy on every call the wallet authorizes.

Part Rule
draw The most USDC that may move from the pool into this wallet. Returned funds can be drawn again. Checked by the pool.
providers Addresses paid per call (x402 resource servers, data/RPC APIs), with a per-transfer cap and a total cap
recipients Plain transfers, such as another agent's wallet or a treasury, with their own per-transfer and total caps
calls Other contract functions the wallet may call, optionally with a cap on one amount argument. Empty by default.
expiry A ledger number. From then on, payments and calls are refused. Returning funds still works.

A USDC transfer passes only if all of these hold: it's the pool's USDC contract, the function is transfer, 0 < amount ≤ per-transfer cap, the list's running total stays within its total cap, the payee is on that list, the current ledger is before expiry, and the covenant isn't revoked. A transfer back to the pool is always allowed.

Everything else is refused: approve or transfer_from on USDC, calls on the wallet itself, unlisted contracts, muxed M… payees.

The covenant doesn't trust the payment rail, it trusts the allowlist. An x402 payment and a direct transfer look the same on-chain, and both are judged by payee and amount.

Lifecycle

Owner (signed by the pool owner):

Function Effect
fund(amount) Locks USDC in the pool
create_agent(agent_pubkey, draw_limit, covenant) Deploys the agent's wallet with its covenant. Fails if total draw limits would exceed what's locked.
amend(agent, draw_limit, amendment) Changes numeric limits and expiry. Can't go below what the agent already drew, or break the pool's invariant.
revoke(agent, by) Freezes the agent's payments and calls, and its children's. Returning funds keeps working.
return_funds(agent, by, amount) Pulls USDC from the agent's wallet back into the pool, using the allowance
close(agent, by) Final. Recovers what's left in the wallet, settles what was spent, and releases the unused draw limit.
withdraw(amount) Takes back USDC no draw limit is backing
close_pool() Permanent. Only when every agent is closed. Remaining USDC returns to the owner.
resolve_dispute(agent, outcome) Records the owner's ruling on a dispute

Agent (signed by the agent's wallet, so its covenant applies too):

Function Effect
draw(agent, amount) Pool → agent wallet, within the draw limit
return_funds(agent, agent, amount) Agent wallet → pool. Always allowed, even after expiry or revocation.
settle(agent) Asks the owner to close it
dispute(agent, by, evidence_hash) Records an objection on-chain. Nothing moves automatically.
delegate(parent, child_pubkey, child_draw_limit, child_covenant) Creates a child agent (see below)

Delegation

An agent can create a child with a narrower covenant, carved out of its own remaining allowance:

  • The child's draw limit is at most the parent's draw_limit − drawn, and it is deducted from the parent.
  • The child's payees, calls and caps must be a subset of the parent's, and its expiry can't be later.
  • Revoking a parent revokes all of its children. A parent can revoke and close its own children.
  • When a child is closed, its draw limit returns to the parent, not to the pool.

Guarantees

Each of these has a test that fails if the rule breaks:

  1. The sum of active draw limits never exceeds the USDC locked in the pool.
  2. No agent draws more than its draw limit.
  3. A transfer is refused for: wrong asset, payee on no list, zero or negative amount, over the per-transfer cap, over the list total, after expiry, when revoked.
  4. A contract call is refused if it isn't listed, exceeds its capped argument, is after expiry or the agent is revoked.
  5. Only the owner can call owner functions; only the agent can call agent functions.
  6. A revoked agent can't draw, and neither can its children.
  7. A child covenant can't exceed its parent on any dimension.
  8. Returning funds to the pool works after expiry and after revocation.

Amounts

USDC has 7 decimals: 1 USDC = 10,000,000 base units. The contracts and the SDK use base units; kovan.mjs and the signing page take USDC ("0.5", "100").

pages.title: Agent tool
pages.description: kovan.mjs, the one-file tool agents use to set up pools and agents and to spend.
pages.html:
Agent tool: kovan.mjs

One self-contained Node.js file (Node 20+). Agents use it to prepare every Kovan transaction. Owner actions are approved by the person in Freighter; agent actions are signed with the agent's own key.

  • Installed with the Kovan skill: skills/kovan/scripts/kovan.mjs
  • Or download it: curl -fsSO https://kovan-protocol.vercel.app/kovan.mjs
  • node kovan.mjs --help lists every command.

Contract IDs and code hashes are built into the file from deployments/testnet.json. Nothing passed on the command line can change them.

Use the rebuilt tool for the native-mandate release: new creation selects current_release, while existing pools retain their verified original bindings. New accounts require a grant before payment; old accounts do not upgrade automatically.

Output

  • stdout: exactly one JSON line per command, e.g. {"v":1,"fn":"fund","status":"SUCCESS","tx":"…","pool":"C…"}
  • stderr: progress, and the approval link
  • Exit codes: 0 success · 1 refused or failed on-chain · 2 bad usage
  • Amounts: USDC (100, 0.25), at most 7 decimals

How owner approval works

For connect and every owner … command, the tool:

  1. Validates the request and builds and simulates the transaction (refusals stop here).
  2. Serves a small page on http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<random> and tries to open it.
  3. Waits. The person opens the page in the browser where Freighter is installed and approves.
  4. Checks that what was signed is exactly the transaction it prepared, submits it, and prints the result.

The page only accepts answers from itself (same origin, random path, single use). It refuses if Freighter is on another account or network. The person should check Freighter's own window: it shows the real contract call, amounts and addresses.

Options: --port N (default random), --no-open (only print the link), --timeout-min N (default 15).

The page lives on the person's computer, so this works when the agent runs on that machine. Cloud agents use the hosted signing page.

Commands

connect

Gets the person's address. They sign a short message in Freighter (no transaction, no fee); the tool verifies the signature.

{"v":1,"fn":"connect","address":"G…","verified":true}

owner <action> --owner G… [flags]

Action Flags Does
trustline Lets the wallet hold testnet USDC. Moves no money.
create_pool New pool owned by --owner. Result includes pool.
fund --pool --amount Locks USDC in the pool
create_agent --pool --agent-key --draw-limit, --providers + --provider-per-transfer-cap + --provider-total-cap and/or --recipients + --recipient-per-transfer-cap + --recipient-total-cap, --expiry-hours (default 24, max 720) Creates an agent wallet. Result includes agent. Lists are comma-separated, at most 10 each.
revoke --pool --agent Freezes the agent's payments and calls
return_funds --pool --agent --amount Pulls USDC from the agent wallet back into the pool
close --pool --agent Final; after everything drawn is back
withdraw --pool --amount Takes back unassigned USDC
create_mandate --pool --agent --mandate-id HEX --intent-hash HEX --expiry-ledger N, plus scope flags below Owner approves a payment grant
revoke_mandate --pool --agent --mandate-id HEX Permanently revoke a grant, without blocking returns

--agent-key takes the agent's public key (G… or 64 hex characters). A secret key is refused with a warning.

Mandate scopes: --scope exact --payee G… --amount 0.01 --reference HEX authorizes one purchase; --scope budget --payees G…,G… --per-payment-cap 0.1 --total-cap 1 authorizes multiple purchases within limits. Hashes are nonzero 32-byte hex; expiry is a future ledger no later than the covenant. Grants never expand covenant permissions.

agent <draw|pay|return> --pool C… --agent C… --amount N [--to G…]

Signed with the agent's key: --key <stellar identity> (read with stellar keys secret) or KOVAN_AGENT_SECRET=S…. The same key pays the XLM fee from its G… account, so fund it once (stellar keys generate <name> --network testnet --fund).

Action Moves
draw Pool → agent wallet, within the draw limit
pay Agent wallet → a listed provider or recipient (--to), within caps and before expiry
return Agent wallet → pool. Always allowed.

The covenant is checked during simulation, so a refused payment fails before anything is sent:

{"v":1,"status":"ERROR","error":"#3904 PayeeNotAllowed"}

status --pool C… [--agent C…]

New agents require --mandate-id HEX --request-id PERSISTED_ID --reference HEX for pay. Persist these exact inputs before signing; never retry a purchase under a fresh ID after an unknown outcome. Draw/return do not take payment metadata. A legacy pool rejects explicitly requested mandates instead of silently dropping them.

Read grants with mandate --pool C… --agent C… --mandate-id HEX, and receipts with receipt --pool C… --agent C… --request-id PERSISTED_ID. A receipt proves authorized transfer, not delivery. Missing receipt while authorization is live does not prove nonpayment.

Reads the pool (owner, locked, assigned, agents) and, with --agent, that agent's limits, drawn amount, covenant and spend counters.

ids

Prints the contract IDs and code hashes the tool trusts.

Common refusals

Error Meaning
PayeeNotAllowed The payee isn't on the providers or recipients list
PerTransferCapExceeded / TotalCapExceeded Over the per-payment cap, or the list's total is used up
Expired / Revoked The covenant has expired or the owner revoked the agent
ExceedsDrawLimit Drawing more than the agent's remaining draw limit
ExceedsLocked Creating or amending would assign more than the pool holds
NotActive The agent is revoked or closed

Full list: Contracts → Error codes.

Chat agents: setup links

Chat assistants that can't run commands (ChatGPT, Grok, Claude.ai) write one plain link from the limits you give them in the chat. You open it, connect Freighter once, and approve each step; the page creates the pool, funds it and creates every agent.

Setup does not approve mandates. New agents need a separate owner-approved grant in the console or a signing link before spending.

https://kovan-protocol.vercel.app/setup?fund=100
  &agent=name:research,draw:40,pay:G…DATA,per:0.5,total:40,hours:48
  &agent=name:monitor,draw:40,pay:G…DATA,per:0.5,total:40,hours:48

(One line in practice.) Each agent takes comma-separated key:value pairs: name, draw (draw limit), pay + per + total (providers and their caps), send + send_per + send_total (recipients), hours (expiry), and optionally key (the agent's public key). Lists use |. Add pool=C… to add agents to an existing pool. All amounts are USDC.

  • The page validates everything with the same checks as kovan.mjs and refuses bad links with the reason.
  • Without key, each agent's key is generated in your browser and offered as a download, for the bot that will spend. Agent accounts get testnet XLM for fees automatically.
  • At the end you get a short summary to paste back into the chat. Progress survives a reload, so a refresh can't create a second pool.

Cloud agents

If the agent can't serve a page on the person's machine, it sends a link to the hosted signing page instead. The page builds the transaction in the person's browser, so the agent doesn't even need their address:

node -e 'console.log("https://kovan-protocol.vercel.app/sign#r="+Buffer.from(process.argv[1]).toString("base64url"))' \
  '{"v":1,"fn":"fund","pool":"C…","amount":"100"}'

The JSON uses the owner actions above with snake_case fields (pool, amount, agent, agent_key, draw_limit, providers, provider_per_transfer_cap, provider_total_cap, recipients, recipient_per_transfer_cap, recipient_total_cap, expiry_hours) plus "v": 1 and "fn". After signing, the page shows a one-line result for the person to paste back. With an https:// endpoint, add "callback" and a random "id" and the page POSTs the result there.

create_mandate adds mandate_id, intent_hash, expiry_ledger, and scope (exact: payee, amount, reference; budget: payees array, per_payment_cap, total_cap). revoke_mandate needs pool, agent, mandate_id. Amounts remain decimal USDC strings. The page fixes the asset to the verified pool's USDC.

pages.title: SDK
pages.description: @kovan-protocol/sdk: create pools and agents, and sign agent payments from TypeScript.
pages.html:
SDK: @kovan-protocol/sdk

A standalone TypeScript/ESM package for the pool → agent → spending → recovery lifecycle. Node.js 22+ and modern browser bundlers. No backend, wallet dependency, key storage or automatic funding: you supply configuration and signers.

Testnet prototype, not audited. The fixes and current-release examples below use source version 0.2.0, not yet published to npm. The earlier 0.1.0 package remains on npm.

Install

Build a local tarball with npm ci && npm pack from the repository's sdk/, then install it into your application:

npm install /absolute/path/to/kovan-protocol-sdk-0.2.0.tgz @stellar/stellar-sdk@16.4.1

@stellar/stellar-sdk is a peer dependency, shared with your app. Packing builds the package but does not publish it.

Configure

The SDK doesn't load deployment files or pick a pool for you. Pass reviewed public IDs, e.g. from deployments/testnet.json:

import { KovanClient } from "@kovan-protocol/sdk";
import { Networks } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk";

const kovan = new KovanClient({
  rpcUrl: "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org",
  networkPassphrase: Networks.TESTNET,
  contracts: {
    usdc: "CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA",
    policy: "CA2NXNPDGZ674K467K3K2IXV342BTPJ7YJRLVZPT4LCSJS5GHLVSMEN7",
    verifier: "CAEU4VYRTV4ZDHFGCRYQNPN6URDOYLP4TS4OMRAJX5RD7AMLWBTYW6G4",
    poolWasmHash: "857f3a27fda736f842e5b4c548022a05197137650cc49f984dde141287175dc1",
    accountWasmHash: "909b66bf67a425308f832ceadc4aa49ef5862ce256533cec3b8a9e4fdab6ccf4",
  },
  maxFeeStroops: "10000000", // fee ceiling: 1 XLM
});

This configuration uses the new native-mandate release. Build the latest source for deployment helpers: releaseContracts(currentRelease(manifest)) selects new creation; releaseContracts(await resolvePoolRelease(kovan, manifest, address)) selects an existing pool's verified generation for a separate client. Old code hashes alone do not reconcile different policies or account code. Do not point an old pool at the new policy.

Version 0.2.0 checks the immutable policy, verifier, token, account WASM and mandate capability before preparing pool operations. A failed binding read refuses preparation. Only explicitly reviewed pre-mandate releases use legacyBindings: true; it must never be an automatic fallback for an RPC error. Retained previous_releases keep existing pools resolvable after a rollout.

For uncertain submissions, persist the hash and signed envelope before sending and use transactionStatus(kovan, hash) to reconcile without another signature. If resubmission is necessary, use the identical envelope, not a freshly prepared action.

Amounts are integer base-unit strings. USDC has 7 decimals: "10000000" is 1 USDC.

Owner: prepare → review → sign → submit

Supply a TransactionSigner, for example a Freighter adapter:

import { signTransaction } from "@stellar/freighter-api";
import type { TransactionSigner } from "@kovan-protocol/sdk";

const signOwner: TransactionSigner = async (xdr, { networkPassphrase, address }) => {
  const r = await signTransaction(xdr, { networkPassphrase, address });
  if (r.error) throw new Error(r.error.message);
  return r.signedTxXdr;
};

const created = await kovan.signAndSend(await kovan.prepareCreatePool(owner), signOwner);
if (created.status !== "SUCCESS") throw new Error(`${created.status}: ${created.hash}`);
const pool = kovan.pool(created.returnValue as string);

await kovan.signAndSend(await pool.prepareOwner("fund", { amount: "1000000000" }, owner), signOwner); // 100 USDC

Use the confirmed returnValue as the pool address, not the simulation preview.

Create an agent

Only the agent's raw 32-byte ed25519 public key (hex) goes into creation. Keep its secret in your runtime.

const latest = await kovan.rpc.getLatestLedger();
const r = await kovan.signAndSend(await pool.prepareOwner("create_agent", {
  agent_pubkey: agentPublicKeyHex,
  draw_limit: "400000000",                                  // 40 USDC
  covenant: {
    providers: [provider], provider_per_transfer_cap: "5000000", provider_total_cap: "400000000",
    recipients: [], recipient_per_transfer_cap: "0", recipient_total_cap: "0",
    calls: [], expiry: latest.sequence + 48 * 720,          // ~48 h at ~5 s per ledger
  },
}, owner), signOwner);
const agent = r.returnValue as string;

Check r.status === "SUCCESS" before using its return value. Creating an agent reserves its draw limit; it doesn't move funds. Draw before paying. The signer, allowlists and policy are fixed; numeric limits and expiry can be amended. New agents additionally require an owner-approved grant:

// Application-persisted, nonzero 32-byte hex commitments; never regenerate on retry.
const approval = await kovan.signAndSend(await pool.prepareOwner("create_mandate", {
  agent, params: { id: mandateId, intent_hash: intentHash, expiry: latest.sequence + 720,
    scope: { kind: "exact", asset: kovan.contracts.usdc, payee: provider,
      amount: "5000000", reference: purchaseReference } },
}, owner), signOwner);
if (approval.status !== "SUCCESS") throw new Error(`${approval.status}: ${approval.hash}`);

Agent: sign with the agent key, pay fees with any account

import { Keypair } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk";
import { keypairTransactionSigner, type DigestSigner } from "@kovan-protocol/sdk";

const key = Keypair.fromSecret(process.env.KOVAN_AGENT_SECRET!);
const agentSigner: DigestSigner = {
  publicKey: key.rawPublicKey().toString("hex"),
  sign: (digest) => key.sign(Buffer.from(digest)),        // sign these exact bytes
};

const draw = await pool.prepareAgent("draw", { agent, amount: "50000000" }, { source: key.publicKey(), signer: agentSigner });
await kovan.signAndSend(draw, keypairTransactionSigner(key));

const pay = await pool.prepareAgent("pay", {
  agent, to: provider, amount: "5000000",
  payment: { mandateId, paymentId, reference: purchaseReference },
}, { source: key.publicKey(), signer: agentSigner });
await kovan.signAndSend(pay, keypairTransactionSigner(key));

The agent signs the contract authorization; the source account signs the envelope and pays the XLM fee. Here one key does both. prepareAgent checks the pool code, asset, agent membership, signer, verifier and policy, signs the authorization, and re-simulates with the covenant enforced. A refused payment throws there, before anything is sent.

API

Capability API
New pool kovan.prepareCreatePool(owner, salt?)
Read pool.getPool(), pool.listAgents(), pool.getAgent(agent), pool.balance(address?)
Grants / receipts pool.getMandate(agent, id), pool.getPayment(agent, paymentId)
Owner actions pool.prepareOwner(fn, args, owner): fund, withdraw, create_agent, amend, revoke, return_funds, close, close_pool, resolve_dispute
Agent actions pool.prepareAgent("draw" | "pay" | "return", request, { source, signer })
Sign and send kovan.signAndSend(prepared, signer)
Signers keypairTransactionSigner(keypair), or your own TransactionSigner / DigestSigner

revoke and close take { agent, by: owner }; owner return_funds also takes amount; close_pool takes {}. Close children before parents, then close the pool.

New owner methods: create_mandate (above) and revoke_mandate with {agent, id: mandateId}. paymentIdForRequest(persistedRequestId) derives a stable payment ID. Keep IDs and exact inputs across retries; reconcile receipts and unknown transaction outcomes before paying again. Grants intersect with the covenant, never expand it. Intent hashes and receipts are not proof of useful work or AP2 credential conformance.

Lower-level builders (buildOwnerOp, buildAgentOp, buildCreatePoolOp, prepareOperation, simulateRead, signPrepared, submitSigned) are exported too. They don't run all the safety checks above; prefer KovanClient.

Errors and retries

  • KovanError has a stage (guard, simulate or submit) and names contract errors, e.g. #3904 PayeeNotAllowed. See error codes.
  • signAndSend returns SUCCESS, FAILED, ERROR or NOT_FOUND. NOT_FOUND means pending or unknown, not safe to retry. Check kovan.rpc.getTransaction(hash) first. The SDK sends once and never resubmits blindly.
  • A signed transaction must match the prepared hash. A preview's success isn't final success: sequence numbers, ledger expiry, fees and the current policy can change before submission.

Test it

npm test                                         # deterministic, no chain writes
node examples/testnet-lifecycle.mjs --execute    # full lifecycle on a NEW testnet pool with throwaway accounts

pages.title: Contracts
pages.description: Deployed testnet IDs, pool functions, events and every error code.
pages.html:
Contracts

Four Soroban contracts, written in Rust with soroban-sdk 28 and OpenZeppelin stellar-accounts 0.8.0. Source: contracts/.

Deployed on testnet

Latest release, published 2026-10-26: native mandate v1, recovery v1, accounting v3. New pool uses these artifacts; a pool instance still needs owner wallet approval. No existing agents or funds are migrated.

New artifact ID / hash
Covenant policy CA2NXNPDGZ674K467K3K2IXV342BTPJ7YJRLVZPT4LCSJS5GHLVSMEN7
Pool WASM 857f3a27fda736f842e5b4c548022a05197137650cc49f984dde141287175dc1
Agent-account WASM 909b66bf67a425308f832ceadc4aa49ef5862ce256533cec3b8a9e4fdab6ccf4

The verifier and USDC below are reused. The following bindings describe the historical displayed default, not new creation:

Contract ID / hash
Pool (v2, retained default) CDP6UNP5YZ6NIMJ2XVQGYLBUAA5RP2LD7SPIRBP4VTVZLKPKCHFX42BR
Pool code (wasm hash) cc1aadcf38ffeee5d15717e04f48f325024b7a47e57ca1548a8e9d49b731b464
Covenant policy CDEQUCR4OHOQHWPIP5RONRR46G7DTJMFZKNKRIQJCLYACDDZGWKAISD2
ed25519 verifier CAEU4VYRTV4ZDHFGCRYQNPN6URDOYLP4TS4OMRAJX5RD7AMLWBTYW6G4
Agent account code (wasm hash) 25dabe1afc7a1ef93a0bc7b40ffa784e0a70463db91c4b1812fc155768ead2d7
USDC (Stellar Asset Contract) CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA, issuer GBBD47IF6LWK7P7MDEVSCWR7DPUWV3NY3DTQEVFL4NAT4AQH3ZLLFLA5

Anyone can deploy their own pool from the published pool code (kovan.mjs owner create_pool or kovan.prepareCreatePool). The source of truth for these values is deployments/testnet.json; they change if the network resets.

The four contracts

Contract Role
kovan-pool Holds USDC, deploys agent wallets, enforces draw limits and the lifecycle. One per owner (or more).
kovan-agent-account The agent's wallet: an OpenZeppelin smart account with one rule and no admin rule. One per agent.
kovan-covenant-policy The covenant, as an OpenZeppelin policy. Shared by all wallets; state is keyed by wallet address.
kovan-ed25519-verifier Verifies agent signatures. Copied from the OpenZeppelin example; shared.

The policy is a separate contract from the pool on purpose: Soroban forbids re-entering a contract. When an agent calls the pool, the pool asks the wallet to authorize, and the wallet asks its policy. If the policy were the pool, that would re-enter the pool.

Pool functions

Function Caller Effect
fund(amount) owner Lock USDC
withdraw(amount) owner Take back USDC no draw limit backs
create_agent(agent_pubkey, draw_limit, covenant) → Address owner Deploy an agent wallet with its covenant
amend(agent, draw_limit, amendment) owner Change numeric caps and expiry
revoke(agent, by) owner or parent Freeze payments and calls (recursive to children)
close(agent, by) owner or parent Recover the wallet's balance, settle what was spent, release the draw limit
return_funds(agent, by, amount) agent or owner Move USDC from the wallet back to the pool
close_pool() owner Permanent; all agents must be closed
draw(agent, amount) agent Pool → wallet, within the draw limit
settle(agent) agent Request closure
dispute(agent, by, evidence) / resolve_dispute(agent, outcome) agent or owner / owner Record an objection / the owner's ruling
delegate(parent, child_pubkey, child_draw_limit, child_covenant) → Address agent Create a narrower child agent
get_pool(), get_agent(agent), list_agents() anyone Read state
get_config(), mandate_version() anyone New release: immutable constructor bindings / native mandate capability
create_mandate(agent, params) original owner New release: approve immutable exact or budget grant
revoke_mandate(agent, id) original owner New release: terminal grant revocation
get_mandate(agent, id), get_payment(agent, payment_id) anyone New release: read grant / durable payment receipt

The published v3 code includes experimental optional-yield functions, but no matching vault is enabled. Pools start cash-only; publication does not activate yield.

Recovery v1 renews the fixed pool/token allowance before recovering an agent's balance, including after its previous 3,000,000-ledger allowance has expired. Only the bound pool can renew it; no signer, policy or arbitrary spender can be added. The new delegation limits are 16 direct children, depth 4 (root is depth 0), and 17 agents per root family over its lifetime. Closed descendants still count so recursive revocation remains bounded. Older immutable releases do not acquire these fixes.

Native mandates are owner-approved exact-transfer or budget grants with intent hashes and deadlines. New account authorization binds mandate ID, single-use payment ID, purchase reference and expiry. The policy enforces both grant and covenant, recording a receipt atomically with payment. Returns to the pool do not require a grant. Generic calls retain covenant checks; native mandates do not implement AP2 credentials, remote task execution or delivery verification. Legacy pools do not acquire these rules.

Covenant parameters

CovenantParams {
  pool, usdc,                                   // set by the pool, not the caller
  providers: Vec<Address>, provider_per_transfer_cap: i128, provider_total_cap: i128,
  recipients: Vec<Address>, recipient_per_transfer_cap: i128, recipient_total_cap: i128,
  calls: Vec<{ contract, fn_name, amount_arg: Option<u32>, amount_cap: i128 }>,
  expiry: u32,                                  // ledger sequence
}

Events

The pool publishes one event per state change. Use Stellar RPC getEvents on the pool's contract ID to follow it.

Event Fields
Funded amount, locked
Withdrawn amount, locked
AgentCreated agent, draw_limit
Drawn agent, amount, drawn
Returned agent, by, amount
Revoked agent, by
Amended agent, draw_limit
SettlementRequested agent
Closed agent, recovered, consumed
Delegated parent, child, draw_limit
PoolClosed owner, returned

Agent payments appear as USDC transfer events from the agent's wallet address.

The new policy also emits MandateCreated (agent, mandate ID, params), MandateRevoked (agent, mandate ID), and MandatePayment (agent, payment ID, receipt). Query the selected pool's policy, not a global latest policy when viewing an old pool.

Error codes

Errors appear as Error(Contract, #N). The SDK and kovan.mjs add the name, e.g. #3904 PayeeNotAllowed.

Pool

# Name Meaning
1 NotOwner Caller isn't the pool owner
3 NotOwnerOrParent Caller is neither the owner nor the agent's parent
4 ExceedsLocked Total draw limits would exceed locked USDC
5 ExceedsDrawLimit Draw over the agent's remaining limit
6 NotActive Agent is revoked or closed
7 DrawnNotZero Can't close: drawn funds are still out
9 BelowDrawn New draw limit is below what was already drawn
10 Insufficient Withdrawal exceeds unassigned USDC
11 NotActiveOrSettle A child is still open, or there's no dispute to resolve
12 ChildExceedsParent Child covenant exceeds its parent on some dimension
13 AmountNotPositive Amount must be above 0
14 UnknownAgent No such agent in this pool
15 TooManyChildren Parent already has 16 children
16 Expired The agent's covenant has expired
17 PoolClosed The pool is permanently closed
18 PoolNotEmpty Can't close the pool while agents are open
29 TooManyDescendants Root family already contains 17 lifetime agents
30 DelegationTooDeep Child would exceed depth 4, counting the root as 0

Codes 2 and 8 are reserved; 19–27 belong to v3 yield operations. 28 UnsupportedMandate refuses grants for agents without the new capability.

Covenant policy

# Name Meaning
3900 NotInstalled Wallet has no covenant
3901 AlreadyInstalled A covenant is written once
3902 NotAllowed Action not allowed (e.g. approve on USDC, malformed call, uninstall)
3903 WrongAsset Not the covenant's USDC
3904 PayeeNotAllowed Payee isn't on the providers or recipients list
3905 AmountNotPositive Amount must be above 0
3906 PerTransferCapExceeded Over the per-payment cap
3907 TotalCapExceeded Over the list's total cap
3908 Expired Covenant has expired
3909 Revoked Owner revoked the agent
3910 CallNotAllowed Contract call isn't on the allowlist
3911 CallCapExceeded Capped argument too high
3912 SelfCallForbidden The wallet can't call itself
3913 NoSigner No authenticated signer
3914 NotPool Reserved (revoke and amend on the policy already require the pool's authorization)
3915 MandateRequired New outgoing payment lacks a grant envelope
3916 MandateInvalid Invalid grant or payment binding
3917 MandateExists Grant ID cannot be replaced
3918 MandateMissing Unknown grant
3919 MandateRevoked Grant permanently revoked
3920 MandateExceeded Grant budget exhausted
3921 PaymentConsumed Payment ID already used, even under another grant
3922 PaymentMismatch Payment differs from the authorized scope

Smart account (OpenZeppelin, 3000–3018)

Raised by the wallet itself, e.g. 3002 UnvalidatedContext (no rule matched), 3003 ExternalVerificationFailed (bad signature), 3016 UnauthorizedSigner. Full list in the OpenZeppelin stellar-contracts source.

Build and test

cd contracts && stellar contract build && cargo test   # target wasm32v1-none

pages.title: Paying with x402
pages.description: How a covenant-bound smart account pays per call over x402.
pages.html:
Paying with x402

x402 lets an API charge per request: the server answers 402 Payment Required with its terms, the client pays, and a facilitator settles the payment on-chain. On Stellar, the payment is a single USDC transfer(from, to, amount).

Why a Kovan agent can pay

The covenant judges the transfer, not the rail. An x402 payment from an agent's wallet is a USDC transfer like any other: it passes only if the payee is on the agent's providers list and the amount fits its caps, before expiry. A prompt-injected agent pointed at an unknown "paid API" can't pay it.

Paying from a smart account

The standard @x402/stellar client signs only for classic G… accounts. Kovan's agents pay from a smart account (C…), so the payment is built differently:

  1. Request the resource and read the 402 terms: price, USDC asset, payTo (a G… account with a USDC trustline).
  2. Build USDC.transfer(agentWallet, payTo, amount) and simulate it to get the wallet's authorization entry.
  3. Legacy accounts sign an OpenZeppelin AuthPayload. New accounts require an owner-approved mandate and a versioned envelope binding the mandate ID, payment ID, purchase-reference hash and expiry into the signed digest. Both use an authorization expiration within the facilitator's limit.
  4. Send { transaction } as the x402 payment payload. The facilitator verifies and settles it; on testnet, x402.org sponsors the fees.
  5. During settlement, Stellar asks the wallet to authorize the transfer, and the wallet asks the covenant. Allowed: the API returns the resource. Refused: nothing moves.

On testnet, a legacy account paid Stellar's x402 demo endpoint 0.01 USDC this way (transaction). A payment to an address outside the covenant was refused by the wallet with #3904 PayeeNotAllowed, before anything was submitted. This historical transaction does not validate the new mandate envelope through the live facilitator.

Status

x402 HTTP handling is implemented in the Kovan console (dashboard/lib/agent-x402.ts), using @kovan-protocol/sdk for contract authorization. The SDK and CLI do not independently fetch paid resources. The console discovers and reviews a quote first, then requires the same quoteId and a persisted requestId when paying. New accounts also require mandateId; the signed reference is the quote hash, and paymentIdForRequest(requestId) supplies replay protection. Exact grants bind the quoted recipient/amount/reference; budget grants limit multiple purchases. Unknown settlement outcomes must be reconciled before another purchase.

The new contracts have passed a live direct-payment mandate lifecycle with disposable testnet XLM. Live x402 facilitator acceptance for this release remains unverified. The chain enforces hashes and spending rules, not URL contents, work quality or refunds. This is native Kovan authorization, not AP2 credential conformance.

pages.title: Security model
pages.description: What Kovan enforces on-chain, what you trust, and what it does not cover.
pages.html:
Security model

Testnet prototype. Not audited. Don't use it with real funds.

Enforced on-chain

  • Total exposure is capped. The sum of all agents' draw limits never exceeds what the pool holds. Only drawn amounts ever leave the pool.
  • Each agent is capped. An agent can't draw more than its limit, and its wallet can't pay anyone outside its lists, more than its caps, after expiry, or after revocation.
  • Rules can't be changed by the agent. The wallet has one rule and no admin rule. Nobody can add a signer, change allowlists or remove the policy. The policy refuses calls on the wallet itself and approve / transfer_from on USDC, so the recovery allowance can't be abused.
  • The owner can always stop and recover. Revoking freezes payments immediately (and the agent's children). Funds can always be returned to the pool, by the agent or by the owner without the agent's key.
  • Edge cases are tested. Zero and negative amounts, muxed payees, non-integer arguments, the exact expiry ledger, delegation that would exceed the parent. Each rule has a test that fails if it breaks.

What you trust

You trust Because
Your owner key (Freighter) It funds the pool and approves every owner action
Each agent's key Whoever holds it can spend, but only inside that agent's covenant
The deployed contract code Tools pin trusted code hashes; check them against the source
Your RPC endpoint Reads (balances, status) come from it; transactions are verified by the network
The USDC issuer USDC's issuer can freeze accounts. While a pool, wallet or payee is frozen, transfers involving it fail.

Keys

  • Owner keys stay in your wallet. kovan.mjs and the signing pages ask Freighter to sign; they never see your secret.
  • Agent keys are created where the agent runs (stellar keys generate) and never leave it. Only the public key goes on-chain.
  • Never paste a secret key into a chat, a link or a file in the repository. The signing page and kovan.mjs refuse secret keys where a public key belongs.

Approving transactions

The local approval page is served by your agent, so a misbehaving agent could show misleading text there. Freighter's own window shows the real transaction. Check the contract, function, amounts and addresses there. kovan.mjs also refuses to submit anything other than the exact transaction it prepared.

Not covered

  • Refused attempts aren't on-chain. The covenant refuses bad payments during simulation, before anything is sent, so block explorers and chain watchers can't see them.
  • Disputes are records, not a court. The owner rules; no funds move automatically.
  • Covenants don't judge value. A listed provider can still overcharge within the caps. Set caps you're willing to lose.
  • Mainnet, audits and compliance onboarding are future work.

Reporting a problem

Open an issue on GitHub.
